title: Equidistribution of primitive quartic torus packets for arbitrary orders
main_claim: Take primitive totally real quartic fields K (no intermediate field), any order O in K, and any ordering of the real embeddings. Weight the packets of compact A_4-orbits on SL_4(Z)\SL_4(R) attached to Pic(O), including all 16 sign twists, by orbit volume. These measures equidistribute to Haar measure with no escape of mass as |Disc(O)| → ∞. This includes a fixed field with order index going to infinity.

issues.location: additive.tex, Lemma add-nonscalar (nonscalar Fourier contribution) and local-fourier.tex Lemma fourier-shell-estimates
issues.description: These carry the conductor-uniform power saving. I checked them only for exponent bookkeeping, not line by line. Exponent consistency holds: epsilon_F > 2tau+3theta, Delta_F >= X^{1/2}/2 ≥ X^{1/3}, profile cutoff H ≤ X^{371}, and the factors 8^{|S|} are X^{o(1)}. This is a coverage limitation, not an identified error.
issues.evidence: In the field-discriminant split, D_F ≥ X^d forces H ≫ X^{d/6-s}, which is consistent. The scalar-term Poisson completion gives exactly A_phi l^{-2} ∏ d_p(m), and its tail is ≪ A_phi l X^{-C_3/3}.

issues.description: Stark's Lemma 8 is used in paraphrase, as the claim that a real zero β ≥ 1-(96L)^{-1} forces a quadratic subfield in degree 4, so it is excluded by primitivity. I did not re-verify it against the original. The constant 96 = 4·4! matches the usual 4·n! form. A sibling branch flagged the same citation.
issues.evidence: The derived zero-free disk |1-ρ| ≥ 1/(192L) and the bound exp(Σ_{p≤Y} a_K(p)/p) ≤ Cκ log Y for Y ≥ D^{1/4} follow correctly from it.

coverage:
I read in full: packets.tex, rigidity.tex, conclusion.tex, most of exterior.tex, the statements and main assemblies of sieve.tex and additive.tex, the start of local-fourier.tex, and the residue and ball-bound parts of ordinary.tex.

Checks made by hand:
(1) Packet volume. vol(F_U) = 8R_K and the class-number formula give 8hR = √D κ. The orbit count times orbit volume also equals 8hN_O R_K.
(2) Exterior unfolding (Lemma end-unfold). The log-coordinate Jacobian determinant is 2. Eight signs times 1/2 gives the factor 4. The switch from U to U^+ gives d_U. U^+ acts freely.
(3) Proposition end-tube. The dyadic logarithm bounds give Σ(a+1)(b+1)2^{-a-b} < ∞. The strip removal costs O(X^{-τ}(log X)^2).
(4) Entropy step. The tube is covered by O(r^{-3}) balls with r = e^{-λ_a t}. This gives mass ≤ e^{-λ_a t} and η = λ_a/3, satisfying 2η < λ_a.
(5) EKL equal-block lemma (unimodularity via degree balance, a rational commutant field), and the obstruction planes V_b via D_α.
(6) Unramified Euler factors. I checked all five Frobenius cycle types (f, ε): the products ∏(1-εt^f) = ∏(1-t^{f_p})/(1-t) and the mean E b_p = (1-t^3)/∏(1-εt^f) from the joint valuation law.
(7) Scalar trace density: Σ(p^k - p^{k-1})p^{-3k} = 1/(p(p+1)).
(8) The shift lemma for p ≤ 5 and for p > 5.
(9) Support bound: |z_b| ≫ X^{-84} from Δ^♯ ≪ X^{28}.
(10) The global-coset bound of 32 pairs per local-coset assignment.
(11) The final Euler-product step, Σ(a_K(p)-1)/p ≤ log κ + log(log Z/log Y) + O(1), with Z ≥ D^{1/4}.
(12) The Stark disk argument.

Not verified line by line: the nonscalar Fourier lemma, the shell estimates, the density disintegration constant, the proof of the sieve assignment lemma, and the Shiu/Pollack application.
